title: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 1 A Visit From The Lord

sense.text:
We start Revelation at chapter 1 because chapters 2 and 3 go into the messages to the churches, so chapter 1 has to preface it. Look at the map of the Roman Empire: that big patch of blue is the Mediterranean Sea, in the scriptures the Great Sea; at the bottom right is the Red Sea, and from the Great Sea to the Red Sea is where Esau built the Suez Canal in the late 1800s. Rome, Italy, is the boot with the high heel, and right across that part of the Great Sea, Macedonia and Asia Minor, the green section, is the area the next two chapters of Revelation deal with.

“The Revelation of Jesus Christ,” The revealing of Jesus Christ. “which God gave unto him, to shew unto his servants things which must shortly come to pass;” Look at that term, shortly come to pass. The way we read it is not the same context as God sees things: 2 Peter 3:8, one day is with the Lord as a thousand years. That is in God's time, not in our time. And Hosea 6 shows that after two days, 2,000 years, he will revive us, and in the third day raise us up.

To shew unto his servants, with an S. Christians all around the world think that they are the servants of God: Moabites, Philistines, Jebusites and Israelites all think they are servants of God. But Leviticus 25:55 says unto me the children of Israel are servants. The only servants of God are the children of Israel.

“and he sent and signified it by his angel unto his servant John:”

precepts.why: Things which must shortly come to pass: that's the part to look at. “But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.” That verse right there is very paramount to what we just read in Revelation. Christ says things which must shortly come to pass; that's in God's time, that is not in our time. So Peter reveals a mystery here: one day with the Lord is as a thousand years.

Something about that thousand-year period. “Come, and let us return unto the Lord:” So the prophet Hosea says come, let us return unto the Lord. “for he hath torn, and he will heal us;” Meaning he put us in slavery and he's going to bring us out. “he hath smitten, and he will bind us up.” Same thing.

“After two days will he revive us:” Y'all see that right there? That two days is 2,000 years. It is literally saying after 2,000 years will he revive us. What we see here right now, that's online right before us, this is us being revived. Notice the word after: after two days. So if two days has passed, what day is it? The third day. “in the third day he will raise us up,” We're in that third day. We haven't been raised up yet, but we're being revived. The reviving is us waking up to the truth; the raising us up is to the stature we are meant to be, when we rule this world. “and we shall live in his sight.” He didn't tell us what part of the third day he's going to raise us, though we know we're in it because we're being revived. So we're just waiting.

That's a heavy mystery right there. The average will read day and go, two days. Remember 2,000 years ago what happened: Christ died on the cross, was resurrected and ascended upon high. That is why Revelation 1:1 says things which must shortly come to pass.

To shew unto his servants, with an S. Christians all around the world think that they are the servants of God: Moabites, Philistines and Jebusites and Israelites, they all think they are servants of God. But watch what Moses revealed here. “For unto me the children of Israel are servants;” The only servants of God are the children of Israel. There's no Arab servants, there's no Hamitic servants, there's no Edomite Caucasian servants; it don't exist. There's no Chinese servants, no Japanese servants of the Lord. They are not the servants of the one true God.

sense.text:
“Who bare record of the word of God,” The word of God is still talking about Jesus Christ; who bare record of the word of God, that's Christ in fulfillment. “and of the testimony of Jesus Christ, and of all things that he saw.”

Something about John, the Apostle John, often called John the Revelator or John the Divine. In Matthew 4 Christ called James and John and they immediately left the ship and their father and followed him: once you're called, you are called. In the book of John, John doesn't often refer to himself as John; he refers to himself as the disciple whom Jesus loved, and the other apostles referred to him as he that lay on Christ's bosom, meaning wherever Christ was, John had his head right there trying to listen and learn. When everybody deserted Christ on the cross, John stuck by him, and Christ gave his mother to John: behold thy mother. John was on another level of love and admiration and dedication and loyalty. And when Christ told Peter, if I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee, Peter interpreted it as John never dying; John himself clears that up. What it really meant is Revelation 10:11: thou must prophesy again before many peoples and nations and tongues and kings. John will be regenerated and come back in the last days.

“Blessed is he that readeth,” We are blessed when we read the book of Revelation. Isaiah 34:16 says seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read: no one of these shall fail; none shall want her mate. You cannot mate the Bible with any other book, not the Quran, not the Book of Enoch or the book of Jasher. And God's spirit gathered the books we have today. The Apocrypha was in the original King James Version Bible, and in the versions that preceded it, the Greek Septuagint and the Latin Vulgate. King James gathered 47 of the top scholars fluent in Hebrew, Greek and Latin; you Negroes today are not scholars and not fluent in Greek, Hebrew or Latin, so put those other books down. Daniel understood by books: he occupied himself studying, and not one word failed. When you got the book in your hand and you don't occupy yourself with reading, you're a fool. Read at least four chapters a day, minimum.

“and they that hear the words of this prophecy,” One part says read, one part says hear. Romans 10:17: faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God. You got to understand your own particular learning curve. Some of us can read and retain, some of us must hear to retain; some of us cannot sit up late and read, the devil jumps on you and you fall asleep, but if you're listening you can stay awake. Everybody ain't the same, so don't be comparing yourselves to each other. Sisters, you got a big job: the mother of the seven sons in 2 Maccabees 7 endured the troubles of education, because all seven sons were not the same and she had to figure out what worked for each of them. All kids don't learn the same.

“and keep those things which are written therein: for the time is at hand.”

precepts.why:
About the Apostle John, often called John the Revelator or John the Divine. “And they straightway left their nets, and followed him. And going on from thence, he saw other two brethren, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in a ship with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and he called them. And they immediately left the ship and their father, and followed him.”

See, once you're called, you are called. Once Christ said follow me, they up and dropped everything. The spirit checked in them that this is him, just like John the Baptist said, behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world. So when they got the call they didn't if, and or but, they didn't give no kind of excuses. John dropped everything and came and followed Christ.

“The first day of the week cometh Mary Magdalene early, when it was yet dark, unto the sepulchre, and seeth the stone taken away from the sepulchre. Then she runneth, and cometh to Simon Peter, and to the other disciple, whom Jesus loved,” Stop right there. What you're going to notice in the book of John: John doesn't often refer to himself as John. He refers to himself as the disciple whom Jesus loved. The other apostles, when they spoke about John, would always reference him as he that lay on Christ's bosom, meaning wherever Christ was, John had his head right there trying to listen and learn.

“and saith unto them, They have taken away the Lord out of the sepulchre, and we know not where they have laid him. Peter therefore went forth, and that other disciple, and came to the sepulchre. So they ran both together: and the other disciple did outrun Peter, and came first to the sepulchre.” Peter probably had a little belly on him, so John ran quicker than him. “And he stooping down, and looking in, saw the linen clothes lying; yet went he not in.”

Why they always said John was the one Christ loved. Remember Peter denied Christ; when he was on the cross everybody deserted Christ. But watch this. “Now there stood by the cross of Jesus his mother, and his mother’s sister, Mary the wife of Cleophas, and Mary Magdalene. When Jesus therefore saw his mother, and the disciple standing by, whom he loved,” This is John. “he saith unto his mother, Woman, behold thy son!” So Christ said to his mother to look at John: behold your son, he's going to take care of you now.

“Then saith he to the disciple, Behold thy mother!” John was the only one there; everybody else took off running, John stuck by Christ. So now he says to John, behold your mother, meaning my mother is now your mother. “And from that hour that disciple took her unto his own home.” That's why the scriptures always made reference to John whom Christ loved. They all loved Christ, don't get me wrong, but John was on another level of love and admiration and dedication and loyalty.

“Then Peter, turning about, seeth the disciple whom Jesus loved following;” So Peter's walking with Christ, they're having a personal conversation, Peter looks back and sees John following. What the hell is this? John is following them. “which also leaned on his breast at supper, and said, Lord, which is he that betrayeth thee? Peter seeing him saith to Jesus, Lord, and what shall this man do?” Meaning this guy that's following us, what shall he do?

“Jesus saith unto him, If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee? follow thou me.” Tarry means to wait: if I will that he wait till I come, till I return, what is that to thee? You follow me, Peter, don't worry about John. “Then went this saying abroad among the brethren, that that disciple should not die: yet Jesus said not unto him, He shall not die; but, If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee?” So Peter had interpreted that as John is never going to die. John clears it up: that's not what Christ said.

“This is the disciple which testifieth of these things, and wrote these things: and we know that his testimony is true.” Many times you'll read and ask who's the disciple that Christ loved; it's telling you right here in verse 24. “And there are also many other things which Jesus did, the which, if they should be written every one, I suppose that even the world itself could not contain the books that should be written. Amen.” So the New Testament is simply an abbreviation; the four gospels are an abbreviated chronicle of the life of Christ. John said the world could not contain what Christ did.

Now what Christ really meant by tarry till I come: Revelation 10:11.

Here's the precept to understand what Christ meant when he said if I will that he tarry till I come. “And he said unto me,” The me is John. “Thou must prophesy again before many peoples, and nations, and tongues, and kings.” Meaning John would be rejuvenated, regenerated, and come back in the last days. Put that in your pipe and smoke it. People think, oh no, there's no such thing as regeneration. Hell yes it is; you're insane. When you read about John's life, he died on the island of Patmos. He didn't come again and do all of this back then. He will come again in the last days, in these last days.

Blessed is he that readeth; this is one we often read. “Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read:” Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, which is the Bible as we call it today, and read. “no one of these shall fail,” What is he talking about? Solomon explains in 1 Kings 8:56: there hath not failed one word of all his good promise. Remember Christ said to John, blessed is he that readeth. Read; no one of these prophecies shall fail.

“none shall want her mate:” You cannot mate the Bible with any book. Brothers, I warn you about the Quran. In Sierra Leone, a Muslim country, we were trashing the Quran and then read out of the Quran that the children of Israel are God's people, and one of the Muslims said, you just said the Quran is garbage, yet you read something true from it, so which is it? We got hemmed up there, but we tore him up anyway. The Quran don't hold no water. It says seek ye out of the book of the Lord and read, not seek ye out of the Quran and read.

“for my mouth it hath commanded,” God's mouth commanded. “and his spirit it hath gathered them.” God's spirit is the one that gathered, because many times people say, how come only these books were gathered? God's spirit had it so for these last days. He said hold fast till I come; he has given us enough of what we need. The Apocrypha was in the original King James Version Bible, and not just that version: the versions that preceded it, the Greek Septuagint and the Latin Vulgate, had the Apocrypha too, the same books. But you got brothers and sisters that go, I'm going to do my own research and find other books. King James gathered 47 of the top scholars who were fluent in Hebrew, Greek and Latin. You Negroes today: number one, you're not a scholar, and you're not fluent in Greek, Hebrew or Latin, so do yourselves and everybody around you a favor and put it down. They go, I did my research, the Book of Enoch, the book of Jasher; one of them little stupid books says Esau was forgiven and God accepted him, and you can't see that contradicts the Bible. They can't see it, because now they got all kinds of folks in that congregation, half of them married to white women. You barely left out of high school and now you're doing research in books written in Greek and Latin and Hebrew, getting all confused, then you want to go on a TV show and battle an Edomite who speaks fluent Greek and get humiliated, because you want to dabble in something you have no idea about. You don't know languages; you barely speak English.

No one of these shall fail: Solomon explains it. “Blessed be the Lord, that hath given rest unto his people Israel, according to all that he promised:” Here it comes. “there hath not failed one word of all his good promise, which he promised by the hand of Moses his servant.”

Many times people ask how do you know the Bible is a true book, it's been published and republished and translated and retranslated over and over again. Simple. The way you know the Bible is truth is Deuteronomy the 28th chapter. Did we go into slavery on ships? You better believe that thing right there did not fail. Did we have yokes of iron on our necks? Not one word of that thing failed. Were our sons and daughters taken from us and given to another people? That word did not fail. Did we become proverbs and byword wherever we scattered? That word didn't fail. Were we removed into all kingdoms and nations of the earth? That word surely did not fail. So we know the Bible is true based on that alone. We might forget the promises, because we're in the curses right now, so we're going to use them curses to our advantage and reveal that them curses only fit our people, and not one word that God said through Moses has failed.

And if somebody can't see Deuteronomy 28, leave them alone. They got to be dumb as a rock. If you can't see that we went into slavery on ships historically, you're an idiot, a walking talking idiot, and I'm wasting my time talking to you. The only way you can disprove the Bible is to prove that slavery never happened to our people. That's the only way.

Another one on reading. “In the first year of his reign I Daniel understood by books the number of the years, whereof the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet, that he would accomplish seventy years in the desolations of Jerusalem.” Daniel said, I Daniel understood by books. What books was he reading? The previous books of the previous prophets. Daniel occupied himself studying, so he said, based upon the writings of Jeremiah we're going to be in Babylon 70 years. And it was so, and it was true, and not one word failed: it was 70 years to the day that that captivity was, and then Persia took over.

So when you got the book in your hand or in your house and you don't occupy yourself with reading, you're a fool. This is why: read at least four chapters a day. At least, minimum; that's a minimum, four chapters a day.

One part says read, one part says hear. We did the reading already; let's talk about the hearing. Hearing is good; hearing builds faith. Many times you men and women ask, how do I build my faith? Paul gave you the secret. “So then faith cometh by hearing,” Faith comes by what? By hearing. Just like your children will know every Barney song, every Sesame Street song. When I was young they had Schoolhouse Rock: I'd be taking a test and I'll be like, conjunction junction, what's your function; I'm just a bill, sitting here on Capitol Hill. I learned by hearing. Me just reading, I couldn't retain it, but through music, through hearing, I retained it.

“and hearing by the word of God.” In case you're confused about what you should be hearing to build your faith, he says hearing by the word of God. You got to understand your own particular learning curve. Some of you can read and retain; some of us cannot, some of us must hear to retain. You got to know what works for you. I can't sit up late and read: you ever start reading and the devil jumps on you and you fall asleep? That's the damn devil. But if I'm listening I can stay awake, oh okay, I'm going to write that down, rewind that. Everybody ain't the same, so don't be comparing yourselves to each other; we all got a different learning curve.

You're going to find out with the kids: all kids don't learn the same. The women have to figure out what works for this particular child. That's why a lot of times black teachers are better than European teachers: they invest themselves in the children learning and try to figure out what allows this child to learn, as opposed to another one, rather than say, oh, they got ADHD, just give a medication. No, you got to figure out what makes this child tick, what makes him learn, what makes her learn.

Sisters don't know the big job they got; there's a big job. One sister said, I wish I could do what y'all men do. No, you don't. You won't like getting spit on and threatened to get beat up, or a gun pulled out on you. Sister, stay in your lane and deal with them hard-headed children.

“But she bowing herself toward him, laughing the cruel tyrant to scorn, spake in her country language on this manner; O my son, have pity upon me that bare thee nine months in my womb, and gave thee such three years,” Our mothers used to breastfeed the babies for three years, the first three years of life. “and nourished thee, and brought thee up unto this age, and endured the troubles of education.” Y'all see that? Endured the troubles of education. Out of her seven sons, you got to sit down and figure out what she means by the troubles of education: all seven sons were not the same. Each of them had a different learning curve. She had to figure out, out of them seven boys, what worked for each of them, what got each of them to learn when it came to reading, arithmetic, the scriptures. She had to figure all that out.

sense.text:
“John to the seven churches which are in Asia:” Write this down: Asia Minor. You got Asia in terms of China, then you got Asia in terms of Asia Minor, which is around the Mediterranean Sea. Acts 6:9 has men of Asia disputing with Stephen; in Acts 16 the Holy Ghost forbade Paul to preach the word in Asia at that time, and later, in Acts 19, Paul had turned away much people throughout all Asia; by 1 Corinthians 16 there were churches of Asia. The Lord will sometimes block your way from certain regions, certain countries, certain states: don't go there, there's nobody there yet, I want you to go here. We got to do things in God's time.

“Grace be unto you, and peace, from him which is, and which was, and which is to come; and from the seven Spirits which are before his throne;” Those seven spirits are seven archangels which are before his throne. We went over this last week. As we read down it's going to tell you about them seven spirits, which are the seven lamps of the Lord, which represent the seven churches.

precepts.why: Asia Minor. “Then there arose certain of the synagogue, which is called the synagogue of the Libertines, and Cyrenians, and Alexandrians,” Alexandria was in Egypt, Cyrene was North Africa; both of them two was Africa. The Libertines, from the Bible dictionary: captive Jews brought to Rome by Pompey in 63 BC, liberated subsequently and repatriated to Palestine, where presumably they built a synagogue still occupied by their descendants a century after Pompey's Palestinian campaign. So these Jews came from Rome. “and of them of Cilicia and of Asia, disputing with Stephen.” It says and of Asia, referring to Asia Minor, which is around the Mediterranean Sea.

“Now when they had gone throughout Phrygia and the region of Galatia, and were forbidden of the Holy Ghost to preach the word in Asia,” Meaning Asia Minor. You got to pause there: the spirit did not want them to teach in Asia Minor at that time. At that time. Acts 19:26 proves that sometime later the spirit said to Paul and them, now it's time to preach throughout Asia. But at that time the Holy Ghost said do not go there; now is not the time, there's nobody going to wake up at that time, you have to wait till later. That's why sometimes we want to go to certain places and the spirit be like, there's a block, we can't get there.

“After they were come to Mysia, they assayed to go into Bithynia:” They wanted to go into Bithynia. “but the Spirit suffered them not.” The spirit blocked them: no, don't go there either. “And they passing by Mysia came down to Troas. And a vision appeared to Paul in the night; There stood a man of Macedonia, and prayed him, saying, Come over into Macedonia, and help us. And after he had seen the vision, immediately we endeavoured to go into Macedonia, assuredly gathering that the Lord had called us for to preach the gospel unto them.”

See that? So the Lord will sometimes block your way from certain areas, certain regions, certain countries, certain states: don't go there, there's nobody there yet, I want you to go here. We got to do things in God's time.

“Moreover ye see and hear, that not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul hath persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they be no gods, which are made with hands:” So what does that prove? That sometime later the spirit said to Paul and them, now it's time to preach throughout Asia. But what we read in Acts 16, at that time the Holy Ghost said do not go there, now is not the time, there's nobody going to wake up at that time; the spirit said you have to wait till later.

“The churches of Asia salute you. Aquila and Priscilla salute you much in the Lord, with the church that is in their house.” So they obviously had churches in Asia, churches of Asia Minor. There were churches built up by the time Paul had written this letter.

sense.text:
“And from Jesus Christ, who is the faithful witness,” The Lord gave Christ for a witness to the people, a leader and commander of the people (Isaiah 55:4). “and the first begotten of the dead,” He was the first to rise from the dead, the firstfruits of them that slept (1 Corinthians 15:20), and by his resurrection from the dead we are begotten again unto a lively hope (1 Peter 1:3).

“Unto him that loved us,” That is the love Christ spoke of in John 15:9, as the Father hath loved me, so have I loved you. And that love goes right back to Deuteronomy 7:6-8: the Lord set his love upon us because of the oath he made with our ancestors, our forefathers. That is where that love comes from.

“and washed us from our sins in his own blood,” He is the one that washed us from our own wickedness. Our sins are not washed away because of our quote unquote good works. Our sins are washed away because of the sacrifice Christ gave for us: it is his blood that purges us from dead works, the breaking of the commandments, so that now we can serve the living God by keeping the commandments (Hebrews 9:14). And the only way we overcome Satan and his minions, Esau, Edom, is by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of our testimony, the testimony God gave us concerning Christ, not our individual testimony (Revelation 12:11).

“And hath made us kings and priests unto God and his Father; to him be glory and dominion for ever and ever. Amen.” Revelation 5:10 says the same: he hath made us unto our God kings and priests, and we shall reign on the earth. All these things connect. Revelation 20:4 shows the thrones, and judgment given unto them: they that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, that had not worshipped the beast, the white man, neither his image, that white image of Jesus, and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.

But the rest of the dead lived not again until the thousand years were finished (Revelation 20:5). That is your mothers and fathers, aunts, uncles, cousins, who die in their sins having rejected this truth. Two out of three of us will be cut off and die here in Babylon, and the third part brought through the fire, a literal fire (Zechariah 13:8-9; Revelation 18:8-9). They received not the love of the truth, and God sent them strong delusion to believe a lie, that Christ is a white man who died for all races, that they all might be damned (2 Thessalonians 2:10-12).

precepts.why: We go here because Revelation 1:5 said Jesus Christ, the faithful witness. “Behold, I have given him for a witness to the people, a leader and commander to the people.” The Lord gave Christ for a witness to the people. Christ is a leader and commander of the people. That is some heavy stuff right there.

He is the first begotten of the dead, and the apostle Paul addressed the same thing concerning Christ: “But now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept.” Letting you know he was the first to rise from the dead.

“Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, which according to his abundant mercy hath begotten us again unto a lively hope by the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,” By the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead: the first begotten of the dead is what gives us that lively hope.
Unto him that loved us. “As the Father hath loved me, so have I loved you: continue ye in my love.” Continue ye in my love. That love goes right back to Deuteronomy 7:6-7.

“For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: the Lord thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.”

“The Lord did not set his love upon you, nor choose you, because ye were more in number than any people; for ye were the fewest of all people:” Here it comes: “But because the Lord loved you,” This is the same love Christ said in John 15:9, the same love John the Revelator spoke of in Revelation 1:5.

“and because he would keep the oath which he had sworn unto your fathers, hath the Lord brought you out with a mighty hand,” So the Lord loved us because of the oath he made with our ancestors, our forefathers. That is where that love comes from.

He is the one that washed us from our own wickedness. It is his blood that washes us from our sin. Our sins are not washed away because of our quote unquote good works; our sins are washed away because of the sacrifice Christ gave for us.

“How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works” The dead works is the breaking of the commandments. “to serve the living God?” Right now, because he purged us from our dead works, our breaking of God's law, now we can serve the living God. How so? By keeping the commandments. That is through Christ's blood.

“And they overcame him” refers to Satan, so read verse 9 to understand who he is talking about: “And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world: he was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him.” This great dragon, this old serpent called the Devil and Satan which deceives the whole world, is the spiritual demon as well as the United States of America, Esau, because Esau is the children of the devil. That is not said based on any kind of racist rhetoric, it is said based on scripture: Genesis 4:6-7 shows it. Get mad now, call your mama.

Why does it say that old serpent? Because it is the same serpent in Genesis the third chapter. “and his angels were cast out with him.” His allies were cast out with him.

Verse 11: “And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb,” Stop right there. The only way, brothers and sisters, we can overcome Satan and his minions, which is Esau, Edom, is right there: they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb. That is why we have to give all honor and praise to the Lord for Christ. We are not overcoming on our good works, because the Bible says all our righteousness is as filthy rags. No matter how good we think we is, we ain't nothing.

“and by the word of their testimony;” The word of our testimony is the testimony God gave us concerning Christ. It is not your individual testimony, because your individual testimony is garbage. The second you get mad at the leadership you give us the finger and walk out the doors; we saw that last year. A sister did her ten-minute testimony video, I ain't going nowhere, I'm rock solid, and two days later she was talking all kinds of evil about us and left with the other Negroes. That is where your testimonies are all garbage. Christ said he that endureth to the end, the same shall be saved. Tomorrow you might be a Muslim or a Seventh-day Adventist. God is not looking for my testimony either; he wants to hear the testimony he taught us concerning his Son, and that testimony is more important than anybody in this room (Psalms 132:11-12; Acts 2:29-30).

“and they loved not their lives unto the death.” We love not our lives unto the death.

The law of sacrifice was instituted during the time of Adam and Eve. “Unto Adam also and to his wife did the Lord God make coats of skins, and clothed them.” The coats of skins were to cover them from their sins. That is a parable, a metaphor: it is talking about animal sacrifice. How do we know it is talking about sacrifice? Genesis 4:4: Abel knew to bring of the firstlings of his flock because animal sacrifice was introduced right here. The blood of the animal gave, at that time, the forgiveness of sin.

This is how we know Esau is the children of the devil. “And Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering:” How did Abel know about animal sacrifice? Because of Genesis 3:21; animal sacrifice was introduced there, and the blood of the animal gave the forgiveness of sin at that time. So Abel brought what was commanded.

Watch what Cain does. “But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth,” because Cain brought fruits and vegetables. “and his countenance fell. And the Lord said unto Cain, Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen?” Why you mad, and why your face look like that?

“If thou doest well,” if you obey what I said through your mother and father about animal sacrifice, “shalt thou not be accepted?” Won't I accept you then? “and if thou doest not well,” if you disobey me by breaking the commandment I gave your father and mother to give you, “sin lieth at the door.” Sin is at your door. “And unto thee shall be his desire,” unto Satan shall be his desire, “and thou shalt rule over him.” Satan shall rule over you. Meaning what? Satan gonna be your daddy. Satan will be your father, Satan will be your God. That is what it is talking about right there.

Your testimony is garbage; this is the testimony God is looking for. “The Lord hath sworn in truth unto David; he will not turn from it; Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne.” Meaning of the sperm that comes from you, I will come and sit on your throne.

“If thy children will keep my covenant and my testimony that I shall teach them,” See what it says about us: if we shall keep the testimony that God teaches us. Not your testimony. The second you get angry you are out the door, and tomorrow you might be a Muslim or a Seventh-day Adventist. God wants to hear the testimony he taught us concerning his Son, and that testimony is more important than anybody in this room.

That verse proves there is no such thing as immaculate conception. For your mothers, fathers, sisters and brothers following an immaculate conception doctrine, that is not the testimony God is looking for. “their children shall also sit upon thy throne for evermore.” The only way we are going to sit on thrones, brothers, is we have to follow the testimony God gave about Christ, that he would come through the seed of David. If you have any other thing in your head, this ain't for you: go on back to Creflo, TD Jakes, Juanita Bynum, Joel Osteen, Billy Graham, Benny Hinn. You don't believe the testimony God gave of his Son, that he would come through the fruit of his loins.

Acts says the same thing Psalms said. “Men and brethren, let me freely speak unto you of the patriarch David,” The word patriarch means forefather. “that he is both dead and buried,” David dead and gone. “and his sepulchre is with us unto this day.” A sepulchre is the graveyard, the gravestones.

“Therefore being a prophet,” because David was a prophet, “and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that of the fruit of his loins,” of the seed, the sperm that comes from his loins, “according to the flesh,” That is the proof right there that it is talking about sperm: according to the flesh, not spirit. “he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne;”

So if you have any other testimony than that, you are in the wrong place and this Bible is not for you. You have some Egyptology Christian crap all in your head; this is not for you.
He hath made us kings and priests unto God and his Father. “And hast made us unto our God kings and priests: and we shall reign on the earth.” We shall reign on the earth.

All these things connect; these are the precepts that connect. “And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them:” Power was given unto them; that is the judgment given to them. “and I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus,” They lost their lives. “and for the word of God, and which had not worshipped the beast,” which had not worshipped the white man, “neither his image,” neither that white image of Jesus, “neither had received his mark upon their foreheads,” neither believed their political policies or religion, “or in their hands;” and didn't support it with their hands. “and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.”

“But the rest of the dead lived not again until the thousand years were finished.” You know who that rest of the dead is: your mothers and fathers, sisters and brothers, friends, uncles and aunts that have rejected this truth, these words of these scriptures. They died in sin. Some of the women say, but my mama read the Bible all her life. Yeah, with that white image of the beast on the wall back there. You ain't fooling nobody, sister: your mama was the devil.

Having rejected the truth. That is not talking about during the time of Marcus Garvey, or even MLK; the truth wasn't out like it is now. But now, with all these men and women, the truth is out, so now we can clearly say you heard the truth and you died in your sins. “This is the first resurrection.”

This explains the rest of the dead that live not again. “And it shall come to pass, that in all the land, saith the Lord,” Do you see the word land right there? It doesn't say lands. It says in all the land: that is talking about one particular land, Babylon the great. “two parts therein shall be cut off and die;” Two out of three of us shall be cut off and die here in Babylon. “but the third shall be left therein.”

“And I will bring the third part through the fire,” That is the key: through the fire. That fire is not just a spiritual fire; that fire is a literal fire. Revelation 18:8 shows it: she shall be utterly burned with fire.

The fire of Zechariah 13:9 is a literal fire. “Therefore shall her plagues come in one day, death, and mourning, and famine; and she shall be utterly burned with fire:” You see that fire? That fire right there is the same fire in Zechariah 13. “for strong is the Lord God who judgeth her.”

“And the kings of the earth, who have committed fornication and lived deliciously with her, shall bewail her, and lament for her, when they shall see the smoke of her burning,” They shall see the smoke of her burning.

This explains the two-thirds that are cut off, and the rest of the dead that live not again till the thousand years are up. “And with all deceivableness of unrighteousness in them that perish; because they received not the love of the truth, that they might be saved.” That is talking about our mothers and fathers, sisters and brothers you try to give the word of God to, and they say I ain't believing that crap, I'm following TD Jakes, Creflo, Joel Osteen, Juanita Bynum, Paula White, I don't believe none of that Israelite crap you saying. Because they received not the love of the truth, that they might be saved.

“And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie:” The lie they believe is that Christ is a white man; that Jesus Christ, a white man, died for all races, people and tongues on the planet earth, and everybody can be saved in white man Jesus.

“That they all might be damned” This is the verse that explains the rest of the dead lived not again. Do you see that word damned? So your mothers are damned, some of your fathers are damned, some of your children are damned. That is heavy stuff, but that is what the Bible says. “who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness.” They had pleasure in breaking God's law: I want Christmas, I want Thanksgiving, I want New Year's Eve, I want pants on women, I want pork, shrimp and scallops, damn it, I want white man Jesus. That is what they wanted, that is what they got, that is the lie God gave them.

There is no magic scripture for your mama. The same scripture you got is the same you gave her; she didn't believe it, she didn't believe we went into slavery on ships. There is nothing we can do. Bye-bye.

Those that are damned are them that die in their sins. This is not about the brother or sister that walks by and says to hell with that, because the day you reach out to them might not be the day God called them to wake up. Look at the apostle Paul: he heard the gospel, rejected it day after day and was killing the church, until Christ said today is your day, and then Paul woke up. Everybody has a particular day, month and year wherein we are chosen and called to wake up. So if our people hear this truth and die in their sins, they are damned; but not the one who rejects it today and might wake up next week, next month or next year. Only the Lord knows.

sense.text:
“Behold, he cometh with clouds; and every eye shall see him,” The clouds are the chariots. Write that down. Who maketh the clouds his chariot (Psalms 104:3) is a metaphor, an allegory: it means he travels. It doesn't mean God travels in a puff of smoke. When it talks about the clouds it is talking about his traveling vehicles, what the white man calls UFOs, and that is what the angels are in. Ezekiel 1 shows the wheel in the middle of a wheel, and the spirit of the living creature in the wheels: the spirit and the chariot were connected, they became one.

Every eye shall see him: when them chariots come, everybody is going to see. Like that movie V back in the day, there is an invasion. When he cometh up unto the people, he will invade them with his troops (Habakkuk 3:16). Matthew 24:30-31 says the same thing John said: the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven, and his angels, the living creatures, gathering his elect from the four winds. And the elect is only the Israelites (Isaiah 45:4). There be some standing here which shall not taste of death till they see the kingdom of God (Luke 9:27), meaning when they see them chariots coming.

“and they also which pierced him:” Wait, wait: they also which pierced him. What is Christ telling us? That the men that pierced him when he was on the cross will be back in these last days; they are walking the earth today. In the Roman army you did have Israelites. Wouldn't it be a shame if that was you, and your mind doesn't get opened up until you see the Lord coming in a chariot, and you see yourself standing in your Roman garments with your spear, stabbing Christ in the side, banging those spikes through the hands of Christ and through his feet? We feel better saying it was just literally white folks. But remember, they flogged Christ, and another group put the crown of thorns on his head and smacked him and said prophesy unto us, who hit you. Imagine when you see the Lord, your mind opens up and it is revealed that was you that did that evil. When people say there is no such thing as regeneration, once you're dead that's it: you're an idiot. Stop listening to these Christian white folks; they don't know the Bible.

“and all kindreds of the earth shall wail because of him. Even so, Amen.” Even so: it is true.

precepts.why: The clouds are the chariots. “Who layeth the beams of his chambers in the waters: who maketh the clouds his chariot:” That right there is a metaphor in itself, an allegory. Who maketh the clouds his chariot, meaning he travels. It doesn't mean God travels in a puff of smoke. When it talks about the clouds it is talking about his traveling vehicles, what the white man calls UFOs, and that is what the angels are in.

The clouds are the chariots the angels travel in; Ezekiel 1 talks about the wheel. “The appearance of the wheels and their work was like unto the colour of a beryl:” Beryl is green. “and they four had one likeness: and their appearance and their work was as it were a wheel in the middle of a wheel.” So this chariot was like a wheel in the middle of a wheel.

“When they went, they went upon their four sides: and they turned not when they went.” When you are in a car and you want to turn, you have to make that turn. The chariots don't do that. When they want to go left they go like that, when they want to go right they go like that; they don't have to roll like a car does.

“As for their rings, they were so high that they were dreadful; and their rings were full of eyes round about them four. And when the living creatures went, the wheels went by them: and when the living creatures were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up.”

“Whithersoever the spirit was to go, they went, thither was their spirit to go;” Imagine this. In the Black Panther movie, when she was flying that chariot, it was with her mind; they got that from this. Wherever the spirit of the angels wanted to go, that is where they went. They didn't have to think about it and make a turn. Wherever the thought was to go, that is how these chariots roll. “and the wheels were lifted up over against them: for the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.” So the spirit and the chariot were connected; it was one. When the angel got in, the spirit connected with that vehicle and they became one.

“When those went, these went; and when those stood, these stood; and when those were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up over against them: for the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.” So the spirit of the angels was in the chariot. It is hard to comprehend because we are men, but that is what it is making reference to.

Every eye shall see him. When them chariots come everybody is going to see, like that movie V back in the day: there is an invasion. “When I heard, my belly trembled; my lips quivered at the voice: rottenness entered into my bones, and I trembled in myself,” He was terrified by the visions he saw. “that I might rest in the day of trouble:” Habakkuk said, I want to be resting in the day of trouble; when the day of the Lord comes, please let me be at rest, I don't want to be alive walking around the earth.

“when he cometh up unto the people, he will invade them with his troops.” He will invade them with his troops. That is why you have movies called Invasion, Independence Day, Invasion of the Body Snatchers: all those movies about invasions come from the biblical text, the writings of our forefathers. That is where they get it from, but they make it little green men with big heads and eyeballs, take me to your leader, and here goes the white man saying he stuck me with something. Ain't nobody playing with your nasty behind, nasty white folks.

Invasion. “And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven” Matthew is saying the same thing John said about the clouds of heaven: Christ coming with the clouds of heaven, “with power and great glory.”

“And he shall send his angels” which are the living creatures, “with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.” He shall gather together his elect. There might be a Christian sitting in here saying he is going to gather the elect, that's anybody that believes in Jesus. Isaiah 45:4 says who the elect is.

Who is the elect the angels are gathering? “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect,” So the elect that the angels are gathering are only the Israelites. So please tell the people in the churches, in Creflo Dollar's church and TD Jakes's, God ain't coming to save you; he is only coming for the Israelites. That is what the Bible says. You can throw your money around at TD, Creflo, Juanita Bynum and whoever the hell, Benny Hinn: you ain't getting saved, brother or sister that's following them. They say I'm non-denominational, anybody can come. The Bible says the Lord is looking for the elect, and the elect is Israel. If you ain't coming that way, you ain't coming. Don't say you never was warned; you was warned.

“For whosoever shall be ashamed of me and of my words, of him shall the Son of man be ashamed, when he shall come in his own glory, and in his Father’s, and of the holy angels.”

“But I tell you of a truth, there be some standing here, which shall not taste of death, till they see the kingdom of God.” That is a heavy verse right there. There be some standing here which shall not taste of death till they see the kingdom of God, meaning when they see them chariots coming.

sense.text:
“I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending, saith the Lord, which is, and which was, and which is to come, the Almighty.” Christ is telling you another name: our God is the Almighty. Isaiah 9:6 calls him The mighty God, and that is why he said he was called the Almighty. He is also called The everlasting Father, because the one we thought was the heavenly Father, from the beginning, was always Christ. God appeared unto Abraham, Isaac and Jacob by the name of God Almighty (Exodus 6:3): you read that and think that is the heavenly Father. It is the Father, but not the Father you are thinking of. When they said teach us to pray, Christ said Our Father which art in heaven; the Father he was talking about was not himself but his Father. There is a Godhead in heaven; our little black minds can't comprehend it, but there is a government in the heavens. We read about the 24 elders; you have angels; you don't do whatever the hell you want up there.

He is setting up a government, not a Sunday school church (Isaiah 9:7). Every government has a top guy: that is the Lord, and under him the 12, then the rest of the 144, a structural system. Right now this is proving ground; we are proving ourselves to the Lord and he is going to choose who is worthy to sit in what seat.

Alpha and Omega is Greek for the beginning and the ending. Proverbs 8:22-31 explains why they call him the Alpha, the beginning: he was set up from the beginning, before everything else was created. Christ was the first of the Father's creations, the very first, before Michael, Uriel, Gabriel, Raphael and all the rest. That is why he is the only begotten Son: he was by him as one brought up with him; the Father taught Christ everything. That mystery, the glory which is Christ in you, had to be taught to the northern kingdom because they were lost (Colossians 1:26-27).

precepts.why:
Christ says another name: our God is the Almighty. People keep on playing with the Bible. “For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God,” You see that part, The mighty God? That is why he said he was called the Almighty. “The everlasting Father,” It says the everlasting Father because the one we thought was the heavenly Father, from the beginning, was always Christ. “The Prince of Peace.”

“Of the increase of his government” What is that word? Government. Some of you in here right now think the Lord is setting up a Sunday school church. No: he is setting up a government. The reason we always think Sunday school church is because black and brown people have never been a part of anything great, any kind of structural thing, so we always think low level. In every government there is a top guy: that is the Lord, he is going to be the top, and under him there is going to be the 12, then the rest of the 144 under that. There is going to be a government, a structural system set up. Right now this is proving ground: we are proving ourselves to the Lord, and he is going to choose who is worthy to sit in what seat.

“And I appeared unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, by the name of God Almighty, but by my name Jehovah was I not known to them.” That is some heavy stuff right there. He said he appeared unto Abraham, Isaac and Jacob by the name of God Almighty. You read that and say, oh, that is the heavenly Father. It is the Father, but not the Father that you are thinking of.

That is why, when they said teach us to pray, Christ said pray like this: Our Father which art in heaven. The Father he was talking about was not himself but his Father. There is a Godhead in heaven. Our little black minds can't comprehend it, but yes, there is a Godhead; there is a government in the heavens. We have been reading about the 24 elders and all that; you have angels; there is a government up there. You don't do whatever the hell you want up there.

He is Alpha and Omega, which is Greek for the beginning and the ending. What does he mean by that? “The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old.” The Lord possessed me in the beginning. “I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, or ever the earth was. When there were no depths, I was brought forth; when there were no fountains abounding with water. Before the mountains were settled, before the hills was I brought forth: While as yet he had not made the earth, nor the fields, nor the highest part of the dust of the world.”

“When he prepared the heavens, I was there:” You see that, heavens with an S? Meaning we have our first heaven here, which is the sky; the second heaven, which is space; and then the third heaven, which is where the Lord dwells. He is explaining why they call him the Alpha, the beginning: he was set up from the beginning, before everything else was created. Christ was the first of the Father's creations, the very first.

“when he set a compass upon the face of the depth: When he established the clouds above: when he strengthened the fountains of the deep: When he gave to the sea his decree, that the waters should not pass his commandment: when he appointed the foundations of the earth: Then I was by him, as one brought up with him:” That is why it says he is the only begotten Son. He was the first of the creation, then I was by him as one brought up with him, meaning the Father taught Christ everything. Before Michael was created, Christ was created; before Uriel and Gabriel and Raphael and all the rest, Christ was made before every last one of them. That is why John said about Christ, he was preferred before me.

“and I was daily his delight, rejoicing always before him; Rejoicing in the habitable part of his earth; and my delights were with the sons of men.” My delights were with the sons of men.

“Even the mystery which hath been hid from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest to his saints:” The Israelites. “To whom God would make known what is the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles; which is Christ in you,” So the mystery of the glory, which is Christ in you, had to be taught to the northern kingdom. Why? Because they were lost. They had to be taught the glory of Christ, that Christ came for them to bring them back to the heavenly Father.

sense.text:
“I John, who also am your brother, and companion in tribulation, and in the kingdom and patience of Jesus Christ, was in the isle that is called Patmos,” Patmos is a little island in the Aegean Sea, shaped like a seahorse. John of Patmos, also called John the Revelator, John the Divine, John the Theologian, is the John of Revelation, the apocalyptic text forming the final book of the New Testament. By most biblical historians he is considered exiled there as a result of anti-Christian persecution under the Roman emperor Domitian. Anti-Christian meaning what? Anti-Israelites keeping the commandments. Domitian was related to Titus and Vespasian, the younger brother of Titus, and he became emperor; that dude was wicked as hell. Since the Roman era, Christians and historians have considered the writer of Revelation to be the apostle John, John the Evangelist, supposed author of the Gospel of John.

Early tradition says John was banished to Patmos by the Roman authorities, and it is credible because banishment was a common punishment used during the imperial period for offenses like magic and astrology, and prophecy was viewed by the Romans as belonging to the same category. So Rome considered any type of prophecy in the same category as magic and astrology. Prophecy with political implications like John's in Revelation would have been perceived as a threat to Roman political power and order: Rome had its ten hills and ten allies supporting it, like America today with the ten common markets, so they figured this is against Rome, we have to exile this guy. Three of the islands in the Sporades were places where political offenders were banished. According to Tertullian, John was banished to Patmos after being plunged into boiling oil in Rome and suffering nothing from it: they threw him in boiling oil to kill him and he didn't die. It is said that all in the audience of the Colosseum were converted upon witnessing this miracle, in the late first century during the reign of Domitian.

“for the word of God, and for the testimony of Jesus Christ.” So he was banished there not for being a thief or a liar or a murderer, but for the word of God and for the testimony of Jesus Christ. He was exiled for the testimony of Christ, not for his own personal testimony.

“I was in the Spirit on the Lord’s day,” Wait a minute. Somebody jumps up: it's Sunday, the first day of the week. What is the Lord's day? Matthew 12:8: the Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath day. That is the Lord's day. “and heard behind me a great voice, as of a trumpet,”

“Saying, I am Alpha and Omega, the first and the last: and, What thou seest, write in a book,” So Christ gives John direction: what he sees, write it down. Why? For the last days, for us today. Whatever you see, write it down. “and send it unto the seven churches which are in Asia; unto Ephesus, and unto Smyrna, and unto Pergamos, and unto Thyatira, and unto Sardis, and unto Philadelphia, and unto Laodicea.”

Look at the map of the seven churches of Asia, meaning Asia Minor: Pergamum, Thyatira, Smyrna, Sardis, Philadelphia, Ephesus, Laodicea. Write this down: Ephesus was the capital of Asia Minor. And there at the bottom left, in red, is Patmos, that little island where John was. This letter had to go to these seven churches.

precepts.why: I was in the Spirit on the Lord's day. Somebody jumps up: it's Sunday, the first day of the week. What is the Lord's day? “For the Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath day.” That is the Lord's day: the Son of man is Lord of the sabbath day.

sense.text: “And I turned to see the voice that spake with me.” Letting you know John wasn't asleep: he said I turned to see the voice that spake with me. “And being turned, I saw seven golden candlesticks;” What does that mean? He saw a huge menorah, like the menorah that was in the temple, that giant menorah. He saw that thing on the island of Patmos; he was looking at it. Exodus 25:31-32 describes it: the candlestick of pure gold, with three branches out of the one side and three out of the other. John saw the same thing on the island of Patmos as he stood there and turned to see the voice that was talking to him.

“And in the midst of the seven candlesticks one like unto the Son of man,” Stop. People will try to hem you up: it says one like unto the Son of man, so they say oh, that ain't him, it was like him. No, no, no: that was him. This is written around the year 96 AD, and Christ was crucified around 33 AD, so about 63 years have passed. John has not seen Christ for 63 years. Now he turns and says, this looks like Christ who I walked with; this looks like the man that raised Lazarus from the dead. It is like seeing somebody you haven't seen since elementary school: that looks like him, you might not be 100% sure, but that's him.

Son of man: you can't just run by that. They called him the Son of man because he came from man. That proves he was not immaculately conceived. He came from the loins of his forefather David, as Psalms 132 and Acts 2 say, and now it calls him Son of man. People play games: son of man because he didn't have no father. You simple as hell. Son of man because he had a father: Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph (John 1:45); the carpenter's son, with his mother Mary and his brethren James, Joses, Simon and Judas, and his sisters (Matthew 13:55-56); made of the seed of David according to the flesh (Romans 1:3). He took not on him the nature of angels, he took on him the seed of Abraham, and was made like unto his brethren (Hebrews 2:16-17). He had four brothers; you mean his four brothers were immaculately conceived too? No. Son of man.

“clothed with a garment down to the foot, and girt about the paps with a golden girdle.”

precepts.why: The seven golden candlesticks. “And thou shalt make a candlestick of pure gold: of beaten work shall the candlestick be made: his shaft, and his branches, his bowls, his knops, and his flowers, shall be of the same. And six branches shall come out of the sides of it; three branches of the candlestick out of the one side, and three branches of the candlestick out of the other side:” It is describing the menorah that was in the temple. So John saw the same thing on the island of Patmos as he stood there and turned to see the voice that was talking to him.

Son of man, because he came from man. People play games: son of man because he didn't have no father. You simple as hell. Son of man because he had a father. “Philip findeth Nathanael, and saith unto him, We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, did write, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.” Son of man: Jesus, the son of Joseph.

“Is not this the carpenter’s son?” Isn't this the carpenter's son? Son of man. “is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas? And his sisters, are they not all with us?” He had four brothers, and he was made like them (Hebrews 2:17). So you mean his four brothers were immaculately conceived too? No. Son of man.
“Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;” Son of man, son of man, son of man.

“For verily he took not on him the nature of angels;” For verily he took not on him immaculate conception. Don't keep going by that. The angels didn't come by sex; God just created them, like when he brought forth Christ in the beginning. He took not on him the nature of angels: Christ, when he came, didn't come the way the angels came, when God just created them like that. “but he took on him the seed of Abraham.” The seed of Abraham. Son of man.

“Wherefore in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren,” Didn't we just read about his brothers in Matthew 13:55? He had four brothers, and he was made like them. So you mean his four brothers were immaculately conceived too? No. Son of man.

“that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest in things pertaining to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people.” How could he be a faithful high priest for us if he didn't go through what we went through, if he wasn't born like we were born? In order for him to be faithful and understand what we go through mentally, spiritually and physically, he had to be like us. He was made just like we were. Son of man.

sense.text:
“His head and his hairs were white like wool,” The hair on his head and the hair on his face was white like wool. Get ready: Jesus Christ was not walking the earth with the twelve apostles with white hair. How do we know? Christ was between 30 and 33. Look at the young dudes that age: if they had a head full of white hair you would spot them out quick: this dude is in his early 30s with a head full of white hair on his head and in his beard, something ain't right. But Judas had to give them a token, whomsoever I shall kiss, that same is he (Mark 14:44), because Christ looked like the rest of them. They all were around a similar age, same look; nobody looked starkly different.

So when the churches say that's his glorified state, don't bug out on that. What's your point? You're saying he came back black but he walked the earth white? Give us a scripture that says he walked the earth white; they ain't got one. There are two textures of hair primarily on the earth, straight thin hair or wool afro hair; those are the two dominant hairs. White like wool: wool is the operative word you want to pull out of there. “as white as snow;” It was fully white. “and his eyes were as a flame of fire;” Because according to Genesis 49:12 his eyes shall be red with wine. Write that down; you should know that one already.

“And his feet like unto fine brass, as if they burned in a furnace;” People say oh, burned in a furnace, that doesn't mean he was black. Let's see. Here is a brass bracelet, and a lighter, weak as hell, a Riverdale lighter. Zoom in, cameraman. Do you see it burning? It is getting blacker and blacker and blacker: black like me, black like lava, black like Yuri. A furnace is a roaring fire; you burn that thing and it gets black. That is the evidence, that is the proof. Daniel 10:6 gives the same description: his arms and his feet like in colour to polished brass, and polished brass means brass burned in a furnace. Meaning he was black.

“and his voice as the sound of many waters.” He spoke very loud. Christ didn't speak with a Joel Osteen voice; he didn't talk soft.

“And he had in his right hand seven stars:” The seven stars are not explained here because he explains it further down, in verse 20. “and out of his mouth went a sharp twoedged sword:” The word of God is sharper than any twoedged sword (Hebrews 4:12). When John saw the twoedged sword come out of his mouth, it is making reference to the scriptures, the word of God. That is why when we teach brothers and sisters we must use the words of God, the words in the Bible. You might think his words have no effect, but whoever hears his word, it is cutting them like a twoedged sword. When you make judgments, use the scriptures; bring out the laws of God, and that is going to cut people.

“and his countenance was as the sun shineth in his strength.” Daniel said his face was like the appearance of lightning; he had a glow about him.

precepts.why:
When he walked the earth he did not have white hair. Here is the proof. Christ was between 30 and 33. Imagine the young dudes that age with a head full of white hair; you would spot them out quick: hey, this dude is in his early 30s and he has a head full of white hair on his head and in his beard, he had a hard life, something ain't right with him.

“Rise up, let us go; lo, he that betrayeth me is at hand. And immediately, while he yet spake, cometh Judas, one of the twelve, and with him a great multitude with swords and staves, from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders. And he that betrayed him had given them a token,” Token means sign. “saying, Whomsoever I shall kiss, that same is he; take him, and lead him away safely.” Why did he have to give a sign as to who was Christ? Because he looked like the rest of them. All they would have had to say is, that young guy, the 30-year-old with white hair, that's him; you would spot this dude quick. But he couldn't be spotted; you could not identify him from the rest of them. So Judas said, the one I kiss is him.

“And as soon as he was come, he goeth straightway to him, and saith, Master, master; and kissed him. And they laid their hands on him, and took him.” They knew that was the one they were supposed to get. Many people saw Christ; he was in the temple overthrowing the tables. But when he got around the rest of them, the twelve apostles, it was like, which one is he? They all were around a similar age, same look; nobody looked starkly different.

“Then I lifted up mine eyes, and looked, and behold a certain man clothed in linen, whose loins were girded with fine gold of Uphaz:” A golden girdle. “His body also was like the beryl,” Beryl means green. It is the same description we read in Revelation 1. “and his face as the appearance of lightning,” He had a glow on his face. “and his eyes as lamps of fire,” Genesis 49:12: he drank wine, his eyes shall be red with wine. “and his arms and his feet like in colour to polished brass,” Polished brass means brass burned in a furnace. That is what that means: meaning he was black.

And where Revelation says his countenance was as the sun shineth in his strength, Daniel says his face was like the appearance of lightning: he had a glow about him.

The twoedged sword that John saw. “For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword,” So when John saw the twoedged sword come out of his mouth, it is making reference to the scriptures, the word of God.

“piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit,” That is why when we teach brothers, when we teach sisters, we must use the words of God, the words in the Bible. You might think his words don't have any effect, but whoever hears his word, it is cutting them like a twoedged sword. God says his word does damage. When they walk by saying you're full of crap, the Bible's garbage, just use one word: Esau. You know what they are going to do? Look it up. Esau is a devout believer in research; they have books, they have dictionaries, and they pride their children on knowing everything. You wear a shirt that says something, the only one that pays attention to it is Esau: reading it, Googling it on the phone. That is what they do.

“and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.” That is why when you make judgments, use the scriptures. Bring out the laws of God; that is going to cut people.

sense.text: “And when I saw him, I fell at his feet as dead.” He said when I saw Christ I fell at his feet like dead. Remember, he saw Christ die, resurrect, and then he saw him ascend; that was the last time he saw Christ, 63 years ago. Now he sees him in glory. “And he laid his right hand upon me, saying unto me, Fear not; I am the first and the last:” The first we have discussed. When it says he is the last, that means from the first Adam to the last Adam; Paul explained that in 1 Corinthians 15, but that is for another lesson.

“I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen; and have the keys of hell and of death.” He said I have the keys of hell and death. That is a heavy statement right there. Matthew 16:19 is the keys of the kingdom of heaven given to the leadership: whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth shall be bound in heaven. John 20:22-23 explains exactly what that means: whose soever sins ye remit, they are remitted, and whose soever sins ye retain, they are retained. That is some heavy power right there. That is what it means in Revelation that he has the keys of hell and death: their sins are retained. Revelation 3:7 says the same thing: he that hath the key of David, he that openeth and no man shutteth, and shutteth and no man openeth.

The keys of hell and death are for those whose sins are retained. You did much evil, your sins were not forgiven, because you did not take the proper biblical steps to seek mercy or forgiveness. Then you are on Facebook acting holier than thou; that is garbage. You are supposed to go to your brother and ask for forgiveness, confess your sins to your brother and the evil that you did. And here is a secret: if you do evil to your brother publicly, you must repent publicly. Brothers and sisters do evil to you publicly, then on the side they call you on the phone, I'm really sorry. No: if you did it in private you can go repent in private, but if you did it publicly then you are going to repent publicly. Their pride will not allow them to do that, and that is why their sins will be retained, every last one of them.

precepts.why:
He has the keys of hell and of death. “And I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.” People read that and get confused; John 20:23 explains exactly what it means.

You think you are going to do evil and get away with it? You are not getting away. You are going to join with the oppressor against the sons and daughters of God Almighty and think your sins are forgiven? Oh no. You better ask Judas Iscariot about that thing. Whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth, meaning whatever sins are retained, as John says, shall be bound in heaven; and whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth, meaning remitted, shall be loosed in heaven: forgiven or not forgiven. That is the power Christ gave to the leadership. Whether you accept it or believe it or not, it is what it is. It has to pertain to somebody. Who is it, TD Jakes, Creflo, Juanita Bynum? It has to be somebody in the Israelite community.

This explains exactly what the keys mean. “And when he had said this, he breathed on them, and saith unto them, Receive ye the Holy Ghost:” Here it comes. “Whose soever sins ye remit,” meaning forgive, “they are remitted unto them;” they are forgiven unto them. “and whose soever sins ye retain,” whosoever's sins you don't forgive, “they are retained.” They will be held accountable. That is some heavy power right there. That is what Revelation means when it says he has the keys of hell and death: their sins are retained.

Brothers and sisters say oh no, I'm good, I'm forgiven. You think you are? When you do sins against brothers and sisters in the body, like that brood that ran up out of here, all their sins are retained, all of them, because in order to get forgiveness, who must they first go to? You have to go to your brothers, and they have not done that. All their sins are retained, every one of them, even the women that follow behind them. You can put that in your pipe and smoke it, and don't blame the Deacon, you can blame me.

You read that and say no, I don't believe that, I never taught that in Sunday school. Your Sunday school is garbage. Your Sunday school didn't have the spirit of God, didn't have the Holy Ghost; your Sunday school was made of the devil the Bible speaks of. That is why you didn't understand this.

“And to the angel of the church in Philadelphia write;” And you women calling your husbands out of their name: you better reconsider that evil you are doing. Don't think you are going to disrespect your lord and the Lord is going to say oh, I forgive. Women do that and think they can get away with it because they have Cesare Borgia on their mind: Jesus loves us all, so I can call my husband what I want and it's good with Jesus. The Jesus you are thinking about is the devil's sister.

“These things saith he that is holy, he that is true, he that hath the key of David,” Here it comes: “he that openeth, and no man shutteth; and shutteth, and no man openeth;” No man can shut, and no man can open. It is saying the same thing that he gave to the apostles, the leadership, in Matthew 16:19, and what we read in Revelation 1:18: I am he that liveth, and was dead, and have the keys of hell and of death. That is for those whose sins are retained. The keys of hell and death are for those whose sins are retained: you did much evil, your sins were not forgiven, because you did not take the proper biblical steps to seek mercy or forgiveness.

sense.text: “Write the things which thou hast seen, and the things which are, and the things which shall be hereafter;”

“The mystery of the seven stars which thou sawest in my right hand, and the seven golden candlesticks. The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches: and the seven candlesticks which thou sawest are the seven churches.” That is why back in verse 16, where it says he had in his right hand seven stars, it was not explained: he explains it here in verse 20. Notice this: the seven stars are the angels of the seven churches. So these letters we are about to read in the coming weeks are not written to Michael, Gabriel and Uriel. You cannot write a letter to them; what are you going to do, email it to them? It is talking about the leadership over those churches.

The word angel might confuse some of you. The word angels simply means messengers. Here is the proof, the explanation of the angels over the seven churches: the Galatians received Paul as an angel of God (Galatians 4:14). Know ye not that we shall judge angels (1 Corinthians 6:3) is not about telling Michael and Gabriel what to do; it is the twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel (Matthew 19:28; Revelation 20:4). The handmaid said of King David, as an angel of God, so is my lord the king (2 Samuel 14:17), and Achish said to David, thou art good in my sight, as an angel of God (1 Samuel 29:9). The term angels is a reference to men on earth as well; when you read it, read it in context. And the woman ought to have power on her head because of the angels (1 Corinthians 11:10): the power to cover her head in obedience, because of her husband, the leadership and the men of Israel, as Rebekah covered her head when she saw Isaac.

precepts.why: The word angels simply means messengers. Here is the proof; write this down: the explanation of the angels over the seven churches. “And my temptation which was in my flesh ye despised not, nor rejected; but received me as an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus.” You see what Paul said about the Galatians? They received him as an angel of God.

“Know ye not that we shall judge angels?” You read that and say oh, we are going to be telling Michael and Gabriel what to do. Listen: you ain't telling Michael, Gabriel, Uriel, Raphael, none of them archangels, nothing to do. Matthew 19:28 shows what it is talking about: judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

This explains what it means by judging angels. “And Jesus said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of man shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.” See that: judging the twelve tribes of Israel. So when it says know ye not that we shall judge angels, it is talking about the twelve tribes of Israel. It is not talking about Michael and Gabriel and Uriel and Raphael.

“And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them:” What type of judgment? Power to make judgments over who? The twelve tribes of Israel. That is the judging of angels in 1 Corinthians 6:3.

We are still explaining the letters written to the angels over the seven churches, and that the saints shall judge the angels. “Then thine handmaid said, The word of my lord the king shall now be comfortable: for as an angel of God, so is my lord the king” See what she said about him: you are like an angel of God.

The term angels is a reference to men on earth as well; when you read it, read it in context. “And Achish answered and said to David, I know that thou art good in my sight, as an angel of God:” As an angel of God.

This is another verse that trips brothers up; some of you just skip it. “For this cause ought the woman to have power on her head because of the angels.” Who has a number next to the word power in their Bible? It says that is a covering, in sign that she is under the power of her husband. So that is what it means by power: the power to cover her head, in obedience. Because of the angels: because of her husband, and the leadership, and the men, because the angels is going into men. What if she doesn't have a husband, what if her father died? That is where the men of Israel come in.

This is why Rebekah covered herself when she saw Isaac. She asked the servant, who is this young man? He said, that is my master Isaac, and she covered her head. She had already left her father, miles away, and she wasn't married yet, but she covered her head. Why? Because of the angels, and the angels are a reference to men on earth. That is what she did for the Israelite man.
